summary: Frontend-only retest of the SMS safety fix and the visitor/intent scroll fix, run at 375x667. Build settings: MODE=live, PROFILE=closed_testing, SMS_TEST_CONTACTS empty. Logged in as voicetest2026@example.com with a fake local TEST_c1 contact (+910000000001). window.open and window.alert were stubbed. CRITICAL FIX PASS: on /women/silent-alert, tapping alert-contact-TEST_c1 left window.__opened empty, so no sms: link was opened. The alert said 'Closed-testing SMS is limited to verified test contacts. To: +910000000001'. The status line said 'No message was prepared. Messaging is restricted in this build, so nothing left this device.' Guardian share PASS on blocking: guardian-send opened no sms: link and showed the restricted notice. No destination param was passed, so no backend journey record was created (0 POSTs to /api/journey/status). However, the guardian-sent-banner still says 'SMS app opened — your guardian has been notified.', which is a false claim. alerts/[id] PASS: the alert was mocked with page.route, so no backend data was used. alert-message opened no sms: link and showed the restricted notice; alert-call showed no Simulated alert. Dialler PASS: /emergency call-112 showed no alert and the 'Continue in your phone's dialler' status; Women's Shield hl-112, hl-181 and hl-1930 showed no alert; chat sos-call-112, sos-call-1091 and sos-call-100 showed no alert. Visitor intent PASS: the screen now scrolls. visitor-intent-call-112 moved from y=790 to y=572 after scrolling, a normal non-forced click worked, and no Simulated alert appeared. Regression PASS: Home, the chat SOS banner, the Family Journey hub and Trusted Circle all render with no page errors. outboundGuard.test.mjs flags only the known pre-existing app/pay-upi.tsx:68.

ui_bugs.issue: sendSMS() calls setSent(true) without waiting for or checking the result of openExternal. When the guard blocks the SMS (closed_testing, empty allowlist), the banner still says 'SMS app opened — your guardian has been notified.' The user is told the guardian was notified when nothing left the device, which is a safety and honesty problem. Reference: app/women/guardian-share.tsx:148-151,300

issues: When OUTBOUND_LIVE=true, the disclosure says 'This opens your SMS app...' and the buttons say 'Prepare SMS to ...'. In this closed_testing build with an empty allowlist, SMS never opens, so the copy sets the wrong expectation. Owner should decide on the wording; no wording was changed.

Blocked SMS in a live closed_testing build uses the heading 'Simulated — nothing sent' and the line 'QA mode — no real call, message or share left this device'. The build is not in QA mode, so this text is misleading (cosmetic).
The contact name and phone column is very narrow, so 'TEST_Contact' and the phone number wrap mid-word ('TEST_Cont / act', '+91000000000 / 1').
The floating 'Help' button overlaps the right edge and chevron of the Two-Way Interpreter card at 375px width (minor).

action_items: HIGH: guardian-share.tsx sendSMS: do not set sent/'SMS app opened — your guardian has been notified' when the guard blocks the SMS. openExternal should return a result ('opened' | 'blocked' | 'simulated'), similar to composeSms, so callers can show an honest status. head-out.tsx:289-293 has the same pattern; it is only safe today because ALERT_SIMULATION_MODE=true.
Optional: in outbound.ts, give blocked-by-policy notices in live mode their own heading (not 'Simulated — nothing sent / QA mode') — owner approval needed for the wording.
Known pre-existing: outboundGuard.test.mjs fails on app/pay-upi.tsx:68 (direct Linking.openURL).
critical_code_review_comments: openExternal now blocks sms:/smsto:/mms: that target emergency numbers. In closed_testing it also blocks any target not on the allowlist, including an empty target such as the 'sms:&body=' fallback. This is correct and covers guardian-share, head-out and alerts/[id].

composeAlert: if composeSms throws, the catch still falls through to openExternal(sms:...). That path is now guarded by the same allowlist, so it is safe. However, the success string 'Message prepared...' would then be returned even if openExternal blocked the SMS (openExternal resolves rather than throwing when it blocks).
openExternal resolves silently on a block. Callers cannot tell a block from success; this is the root cause of the guardian-share false 'notified' banner.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested checks pass; 1 HIGH honesty bug found in guardian-share banner copy/state)

seed_data_creation: No backend data was created. The TEST_c1 trusted contact lives only in browser localStorage. The alerts/[id] response was mocked with page.route, and the journey POST was route-blocked (it was not called).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse the INIT_JS and SEED_JS from /app/tests/dialler_restore_ui_test.py. '/' redirects to /home; to reach chat, tap home-type-button, then chat-input and send-button, and type 'help me' to get sos-emergency-banner. To test /alerts/[id] without backend data, mock GET **/api/alerts/TEST_a1** with an object that has owner_phone. /women/guardian-share without a destination param does not create a backend journey record.
rca_of_issue: Guardian share false banner: sendSMS() fires openExternal(...) without awaiting it and calls setSent(true) right away. openExternal returns undefined both when it blocks and when it opens, so the screen has no signal to show a 'restricted' state. Fix: have openExternal return a status, and set sent only when the status is 'opened'; otherwise show the restricted notice.
